quantities.label: Part type rule: a part is Compact when its uncompressed bytes < min_bytes_for_wide_part, its rows < min_rows_for_wide_part or its level < min_level_for_wide_part, else Wide. An insert measures the block in memory (Block::bytes); a merge sums the inputs' on-disk uncompressed column bytes, uses level max(input levels) + 1, and is Wide when any input is Wide. quantities.label: Upload sizing: with strict_upload_part_size = 0 WriteBufferFromS3 fills a first buffer of clamp(max_single_part_upload_size, min_upload_part_size, max_upload_part_size), then buffers of min_upload_part_size that grow by multipart_growth_factor every multipart_growth_parts buffers (up to 5 GiB); with a strict size every buffer is that size. A second filled buffer starts the multipart upload. At finalize one buffer of at most max_single_part_upload_size is one PutObject (an object of exactly 32 MiB by default); one larger buffer, possible only when the first buffer or the strict size exceeds max_single_part_upload_size, is a multipart upload of one part. quantities.label: Async flush: an INSERT with data of at most async_insert_max_data_size bytes is queued (INSERT SELECT and larger data run synchronously); inserts with the same user, roles, query shape, settings and data kind share a buffer; it is flushed into one part per partition when its unparsed bytes reach async_insert_max_data_size, when async_insert_max_query_number inserts accumulate with deduplication on, or when its deadline passes. The deadline is the first insert time plus an adaptive timeout between async_insert_busy_timeout_min_ms and _max_ms that grows while inserts are frequent. With wait_for_async_insert = 1 a client waits for the flush, so only concurrent inserts share one.

quantities.label: Fetch vs local execution of a replicated merge, in order: skip when the part or a covering one is already here; fetch when always_fetch_merged_part; try to fetch a TTL-recompress merge another replica was assigned, quietly retrying while no replica has it, until try_fetch_recompressed_part_timeout; fetch when execute_merges_on_single_replica_time_threshold > 0, the entry is younger than it and another replica is picked; fetch when a source or patch part is missing or covered; while a source part has newer metadata, try to fetch, quietly retrying; fetch when the entry is at least prefer_fetch_merged_part_time_threshold old, the sources hold at least prefer_fetch_merged_part_size_threshold bytes on disk and a replica has the result; with zero-copy, fetch or wait on the covering part and the exclusive lock; else merge locally. A mutation: fetch when always_fetch_mutated_part, the source is missing or covered, or the entry is that old and 1.1 x the source bytes on disk (expired TTL parts excluded) reach the size threshold with a replica holding the result; the single-replica branch never fires (merge entries only); zero-copy as for merges; else mutate locally, keeping the source part type.
